answer: I ran the 3-qubit GHZ circuit on sirius:mock with 200 shots. The circuit was H on q0, CNOT q0 to q1, CNOT q1 to q2, then a measurement of all 3 qubits. I submitted one job with the iqm_run.py helper. Its ID is 01a15f16-f6bf-7133-9d7f-5c450cbfaf8d. The job completed with no errors. The transpiler turned the circuit into 5 r gates, 2 cz gates, 4 move gates and 3 measurements. Sirius is a Star QPU, so it routes qubit interactions through a resonator with MOVE gates. The counts were {"000": 200}. All 200 shots came back as 000. This is the mock backend. A mock does not simulate quantum physics, so these counts do not show real GHZ behavior. A real QPU would give mostly 000 and 111. The mock cost no credits (estimated_credits 0.0). The QASM file is /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_1a6926f8-f6c-28/ghz3.qasm.
